key_insight: LLM-agent collaboration can be modeled as block optimization with provable linear convergence to an error floor that vanishes when cross-agent corrections are exact.
engineering_relevance: A coordinator that checks proposals against a global objective can turn parallel agent work into reliable progress while safely merging compatible updates.
method: Each agent improves one solution block using a local objective plus a correction for effects on other blocks.
A coordinator checks global improvement and merges noninterfering proposals or explicitly checked combinations.
The convergence rate accounts for how well accepted proposals combine.
evidence_signal: In GPT-OSS-120B robot-routing tests, three agents found collision-free plans in every run; on a larger task, six agents searched about twice as fast as a single agent in median, and merging the best checked combination cut team search time by about 30%.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on the cost of global checks and the accuracy of cross-agent corrections; approximate corrections can leave a nonzero error floor.
paper_title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
